# Reported genotype landscape and database representation

The cohort landscape is defined from governed clinical data that are not committed
to this repository. No synthetic cohort distribution is substituted in this book.
The final analysis should report person- and episode-level denominators, referral
strata, positive/negative/incomplete reports, HBA/HBB chromosome-haplotype classes,
compound states, unresolved nomenclature and calendar-era changes.

The historical positive fraction is a property of an enriched referral cohort, not
population prevalence. Likewise, differences between historical and ONT report
frequencies combine biological, demographic, assay and reporting effects.

## Database representation

Each reported label should be linked to a canonical genomic allele or explicit
structural haplotype while retaining the original wording. Public-database review
should distinguish exact sequence representation from broad interval overlap and
should record transcript, genome build, HBA copy ambiguity, junction definition,
clinical assertion and ancestry coverage. An absent database record can reflect
nomenclature or representation failure rather than biological rarity.

## Evolutionary interpretation

A pathogenic HBB allele alone does not identify a classical beta-globin haplotype.
Founder or selection analyses require linked markers and phase. Where these are not
present in the report-derived cohort, external phased resources may describe known
backgrounds but cannot assign them to individual patients.
